utterances.text: Yes, that's right. So all together it was non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And approximately how many non-Serbs were left in the municipality in -- by October 1995 when the town was liberated?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: On the 13th of October, 1995, we were conducting a census and the population of Sanski Most was 575, 284 of which were Croats and the rest were Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And my last question: What physical or psychological effects, if any, do you suffer as a consequence of the beatings and the mistreatment during your detention at the Sanski Most police station, the Betonirka garage, and the Manjaca detention facilities?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: First of all, I don't have a single tooth of my own. All of these are fake teeth because I was kicked in the teeth. When they throw you on the ground, then they kick you in the face and teeth. I'm diabetic since then and the result of that diabetes is the weakening of my eyesight, as you have seen, and there is the possibility of me going blind all together. Also when the weather changes I feel pain and I feel ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, I'm sorry, the interpreters didn't catch the last part of your answer. You said you feel -- when the weather changes you feel pain and I feel ... what?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I feel pain and I feel -- I feel -- I mean my legs, in my legs, it's hard for me to walk.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions and we could possibly deal with associated exhibits after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or we can do that right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. I seek leave to add one of the associated exhibits listed on the Rule 92 ter notification and that's 65 ter 23453. It's the fifth item listed on the notification which was filed on the 2nd of September. This was discussed both in evidence in chief and in cross-examination in the Brdjanin trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are not adding 23404 -- I'm sorry, 23450 to 23452? My understanding you are seeking --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- leave in relation to those four documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think -- do you have any objection, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that they are part of indispensable and inseparable associated exhibits, we grant it. There are -- any objection in relation to other associated exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, can I draw your attention to 65 ter 00545, which is referred to in the transcript page 6160, where the Prosecution just drew the attention of the Chamber and didn't ask any question to the witness. So you might -- in Chamber's view that it does not form an inseparable and indispensable part of the transcript. So if you find it necessary to tender this document, I would like you to lead the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Did you want to have a break now. I can look at the document in the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And in the meantime, if you could take a look at 65 ter numbers 5022, 5073, and 5090. The thing may be that in relation to these final three documents you are tendering not for the truth of the content of those documents, but just to have the Chamber understand the context of the witness's evidence. We'll take a break for an hour, after which we'll hear the cross-examination of the witness by the accused. But, Mr. Karadzic, with respect to Mr. Robinson's request to extend your time for cross, at the moment the Chamber is not minded to extend your time for your cross-examination. At the end of those three hours, the Chamber may reconsider your application.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, would the Chamber consider removing the cross-examination from the 92 ter package and giving us the five and a half hours that were used on cross-examination because we don't -- it seems like perhaps that's one of the things that has allowed the Chamber to conclude that three hours for Dr. Karadzic is sufficient in the face of seven and a half hours of direct examination, and we don't find that that five and a half hours is that useful to us, given that Mr. Brdjanin was blaming the military, General Talic was blaming civilians, and Dr. Karadzic is charged with responsibility for both. So if you feel that the reason you've diminished our time was because there was cross-examination in Brdjanin, we would prefer to remove that cross-examination from the evidence and use the time in a way that is more consonant with Dr. Karadzic's defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, that's certainly a point that we will reconsider at the end of the three hours, Mr. Robinson. I see the logic behind the application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, I do agree with the comments of Judge Morrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge Baird.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This may be the case that Mr. Karadzic can show us an example that he can be efficient and focused. We'll have a break for an hour and resume at 1.40. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.42 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, in relation to 65 ter 00545, I agree that the exhibit isn't associated. Mr. Cayley simply read in two lines into the record on the back of another document which dealt with events happening in Vrhpolje and Hrustovo. In relation to -- so I don't seek to have that admitted as an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At least with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to 65 ter 05073, at transcript page 6298, Defence counsel read out one sentence to the witness about this Milos document dated the 29th of May, 1992, and he was asked whether he knew anything about the incident of people from the SDA being killed and quite a number of them being captured or arrested. And he said: "I heard about these events. As I said already I was in prison and couldn't witness it myself." So basically albeit hearsay, but he has confirmed what was read to him. So I would seek the admission of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to 65 ter 05090, at transcript page 6253, Defence simply asks the witness to confirm who this Crisis Staff decision of the 6th of June was sent to. And I agree that the witness can't confirm that the Crisis Staff were ordering the SJB to evacuate 150 prisoners to Manjaca, but he did say in his evidence today that five convoys of detainees were taken from Sanski Most to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the position of the Defence, that can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I seek its admission, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And finally in relation to 65 ter 05022, at transcript page 6133, the witness was read the first paragraph of this conclusions of the Crisis Staff meeting held on the 28th of April, 1992, dealing with the fact that all citizens were -- who possessed any kind of weapons should hand it in to the public police station. And he was asked whether he was aware of the decision at the time, and he said no. But then he was further questioned on transcript page 6134: "Were you aware that the population was being disarmed at the end of April? "A. I was. "Q. Were all ethnic groups within the population being disarmed, Serbs, Croats, and Muslims? "A. Only non-Serbs were being disarmed. "Q. How do you know this? "A. I saw it with my own eyes." And then he's taken to another part of the document and asked a question about that, to which he didn't know the answer to. But I think that he sufficiently dealt with the issue of disarming of the population and I seek the admission of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that can be admitted as well. Finally, in relation to Mr. Rasula's diary, is it 65 ter 4988 or 20591 that you are tendering?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I would seek to tender the 65 ter number 04988 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- because that's the certified copy of the larger range of the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we are going to admit only those pages shown to the witness, so could you liaise with the court deputy to identify the page numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it your intention, Mr. Robinson, that the Defence is going to use that document as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you do not object to admitting it in its entirety or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we do object to admitting it in its entirety. We think that it ought to be limited to the pages used by either side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. So if the parties could co-ordinate with the court deputy to identify those page numbers later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just say that this document is going to be used with other witnesses as well, it's not just this witness. So I don't know whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then they can be added later on when you are going to use that document later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I would just note that it was admitted also in its entirety not only in Brdjanin but in the Krajisnik trial as well. Mr. Tieger wants to add something, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was just going to say perhaps we can speak to Mr. Robinson about this further and perhaps come to some consensus about the admissibility of this document and similar types of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit only those pages at the moment and we'll come back to it later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to remind both you and myself to pause so that we do not cause the interpreters any headaches. I wanted to thank you because you were kind as to talk to the Defence via videolink. I hope that this will help us be as efficient as possible and with a view to cross-examining you as smoothly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to start with something that you said today on pages 50 and 51 of the transcript; namely, that you - that is to say, the Muslim community in Sanski Most - were in favour of what was legal and what was lawful and that you were in favour of life together. Do you agree that tensions arose considerably before the outbreak of the conflict in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, I have said that we did not have any problems until the Municipal Assembly of Sanski Most on the 6th or 7th of April. There were tensions but it wasn't major tensions. We sat together, we co-operated. I tell you, I as the number two man, together with the president of the municipality, Rasula, we had meetings every day, working hours started at 7.00, but every day from 7.00 until 8.00 we would sit and have a cup of coffee and consult about our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why then was it necessary for the Muslim community to arm secretly and organise itself for war considerably before the 6th of April?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Let me tell you, that is what you are saying. That is what you are saying. We in Sanski Most did not arm ourselves; we felt no need to do so. Because until then, there were joint guards, there was joint guard duty, the Territorial Defence had distributed weapons to everyone, that is to say, Serbs and Muslims and Croats. The people did feel something, though, and they were arming themselves, at least that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that these guards were organised because of the war in Croatia or because of mutual suspicions and fears?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, it was both, it was both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to call up a document, a book, and I'm sure that you know about it. Zilhad Kljucanin and Hazim Akmadzic, do you know them? They are the authors.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Kljucanin is from a village near Sanski Most and through Zilhad I also met Akmadzic. They are writers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D31, can we have that, please, that is to say, 1D00031. I beg your pardon 1D4253, can we have that, please. 1D4253. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the first page. Do you know this book?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at page 3 of this book. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the publisher the Municipality of Sanski Most, is the co-editor Bosnjak, and then there is a reference here to the board, that includes yourself, Mehmed Alagic, Adil Draganovic, Kljucanin, Lemes, and so on?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? Actually, this is just in order to identify a book which we do not have in its entirety. We are just going to be tendering parts of the book that have been translated. So can it be MFI'd for the time being, that is to say, the front page and the third page, so I'm talking about those two pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see a basis to admit it now. I don't hear anything from the witness except for the author.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, Mr. Karabeg is a member of the editorial board. This is a book that they edited and published. I'm not going to tender the entire book because I don't have a translation of the entire book. This is just for the sake of identification and the parts that I'm going to tender can then be registered under the same number. So what we need is some kind of cover page, as it were, where these other pages can fit in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit those five pages, first five pages, which -- and we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1677.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I don't understand what's on the first five pages that we're admitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll see. The witness confirmed that he's a member of this board. I see that he -- the witness's name --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- and what relevance it will have --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- we can find out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D00031. Thank you. Can we have page 51 now, please, in the book itself. It would be page 4 if it were a separate document but if we're looking at the entire book it is 51. We do have a translation for pages 51 and 52. Actually, can we go back to the previous page in English. I would like to draw your attention to this part in the box, where it says that the SDA started collecting money for the procurement of weapons. In August 1991 a certain amount of money for weapons was collected, you can see that for yourself. I don't need to read it out. So from August 1991 the SDA was collecting money to buy weapons in Sanski Most. And Hasib Kamber is the man in charge as well as Rasim Karabeg. What is Rasim Karabeg to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Nothing. I know him but we're not related, very distantly perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you are from the same family, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, we're supposed to be but sort of seven or eight times removed. Well, yes, my ancestors and his come from the same village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree, Mr. Karabeg, that explosive is not a hunting weapon in any conceivable way?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page and the English translation, too, of page 52. Next page in Serbian -- actually, the previous one in Serbian. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, this is how it continues, Rasim Karabeg and then it goes on to say -- you see it for yourself: "Kamber obtained in late 1991 and the beginning of 1992 a certain amount of explosive ..." Do you agree that one can only use explosives for destruction, that this is a terrorist device?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, you can do all sorts of things with explosives. You can destroy, you can blow up things if you need to do it for your own purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the names. Who else raised funds for buying weapons? And it is the elite of the SDA that is referred to, yourself included, and it is also hodza Husein Efendija Kovacevic and all these names, we can all see them here. And it says here that the ways in which the Green Berets are going to be used have been differentiated.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Let me tell you, collecting money for the procurement of weapons is not the same thing, I mean procuring and buying weapons. What you say about the Green Berets, well, yes, for the most part it was the Territorial Defence where people were arming themselves and where they did organise themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. So we see here that due to heightened police and military checks -- you see what it says here, that communication is more difficult because police and military checks have been heightened and also supervision on the part of the State Security Service and the military security. So it is these checks that made it more difficult to conduct the activity that you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I did not quite understand what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, read out this part that I've just read out.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Can it be zoomed in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am going to read it out. "It is important to point out the fact here that in Sanski Most there was not a clear differentiation as to how and when the combat groups of the Green Berets should be used, primarily because communication was more difficult with the regional centre and the centre in Sarajevo. The reason for impeded communications should be sought in heightened police" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, don't waste time reading out the documents. Mr. Karabeg, can you read the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is: Do you agree that this document clearly shows that checks and patrols were justified and that they were impeding the consolidation of the Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: That is what you're saying. That is what you claim. Checks could not be justified because this is only the Serb side that was carrying out these checks at these check-points. But I am talking about this part, where Sanski Most, Prijedor, and Banja Luka, and Kljuc, and Mrkonjic are and so on and so forth, where the Serb side absolutely took over. That was one of the reasons, one of the causes, that led to the beginning of this instability. You know that full well. A proposal had been made and at first there were joint patrols, but the Serb side did not agree to that. They just wanted to have their own patrols and their own checks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you inform the Serb side about the fact that you had established the Green Berets, that you had purchased 2 tonnes of explosive and weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of 2 tonnes of explosives are you talking about, what kind of weapons are you talking about? I am saying that in Vrhpolje and Hrustovo people had organised themselves. But informing someone about something, whoever wants to do things legally and these others are doing it illegally and destroying everything, I think that that is absurd. You are now trying to say that we -- I mean when I say "we," it's not Bosniaks. You are trying to say that we did what you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry, I was not clear and so I'm asking you, Mr. Karabeg, again. According to this book, you are referred to as having participated in the raising of funds and collection of arms and you also -- you referred to -- you said that collecting money for the procurement of weapons is not the same thing. But you agree that you participated in collecting money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said that and, if I may add, the weapons that were bought were bought from the Serbs, who sold dysfunctional weapons. And when they asked for the weapons to be returned, he knew which piece of weaponry was located with what person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karabeg. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the bottom part where it is stated that in early 1992, before the war, it says that around 900 Bosniaks were armed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I don't know how many there were in Vrhpolje and Hrustovo. I know that there were around 170 of them when they took prisoners -- prisoner those Serbs, but I believe that those who remained were arrested by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we're talking now about the period of 1992 three months before the war, where it says that 900 Bosniaks were armed. And this is the book that you helped edit and released for publication the way it is now; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying that it is possible this was the case because people were arming themselves independently, illegally, and you did everything legally. You had the territorial weapons and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is precisely what puzzled me because you said earlier on that you were the ones doing everything legally and the Serbs illegally. And now it turns out that the Serbs had weapons legally, through the TO, and the Muslims were the ones arming illegally. This is what you just said, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to the text in the box. It says that the most important activity during that period of time was that of intelligence and that Serb policemen knew everything that was being done and who it was done by. And then you also mention the municipalities like Vrhpolje, Trnovo, Hrustovo, Sehovci, Kamengrad, and then the towns neighbourhoods of Mahala and Muhic, all of which were armed. So we're talking about the local communes that were further away from the town proper, whereas the neighbourhoods of Mahala and Muhici were part of town?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the lower box.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, I can't read it properly. Are you talking about the read line, the red box?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: This is fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Mahala in the very centre of the town, part of the town, and Muhici is on the periphery, is it a suburb?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the third paragraph from the top where it is stated that a meeting was held where the Serbs asked for their organs -- and it is stated there that following this meeting, Mirzet Karabeg went to the Sanski Most Municipal Assembly, the Serbs and -- the Muslims and the Croats and said that they had legal state organs behind them. Is that right, there was a division within the police force, the Serbs asked for two police stations, two Municipal Assemblies, and listed what in their view was to constitute the municipality of Sanski Most. And then you went on to say that the Muslim and Croat part of the police force was the legitimate power behind this police station?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't the term "police" that was used at the time, rather, it was "milicija," and our police force was driven out of the police station to the fire brigade premises. And when we left this meeting where attempts were made at resolving the issue, they did not want to agree to any other discussion but that we should pledge loyalty to the Serbs, embrace the Serb flag, et cetera. I was the president of the Executive Board at the time and I left the police building with Redzo for the municipal building, where I heard that our police force had been chased away and was now housed in the fire brigade building. At that point we decided to invite them to join us in the municipal building. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, they were not chased away. Rather, they were offered that they should form a Muslim-Croat police station within the fire brigade building. Now, let me ask you this: Was Mr. Rasula a man number one in the municipality of Sanski Most, was he not the president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes, he was the man in charge because the man in charge in a municipality is the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it not the case that under our Law on All People's Defence a president of the municipality is ex officio the president of the defence council for a municipality and commander of the Territorial Defence, meaning its supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: This was the case indeed up until the tensions emerged on the 6th and the 7th of April. I as the president of the Executive Board dealt with these issues which were subsequently taken over by the president of the municipality. Because under the regulations in force, I was the person in charge of the executive government and he was in charge of the legislative branch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can Mr. Karadzic please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karabeg, because of the overlapping, the interpreters were not able to catch what you were just talking about. So could you start from your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question was, which Mr. Karabeg affirmed, whether the president of the municipality was, under the prevailing system, the person in charge in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. This person who was in charge was man number one. Was he also not in favour of having the Muslim and Croat policemen proclaimed as the legitimate police force?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Which police force do you mean, the Serb police force? Which legitimate force of milicija?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say or the book says that Kurbegovic and you went and told the Muslims and Croats in the fire brigade building that they were the legitimate police force and that legitimate state organs were backing them up and Rasula was not backing them.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: No. Well, Rasula was the person who was mostly in favour of the divide in the police force. He was the person undermining the whole system.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have pages 50 through 55 of this document admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll add these pages from pages 51 to 55 to the previous one which has been marked for identification. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I forgot to mention to you, Mr. Karadzic, given that this is translated only partially, we need a full translation. That's part of the reason we put it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in mid-March in the building of the Islamic religious community a meeting took place between the leadership of the SDA of Sanski Most with Mr. Osman Brka, high official of the Main Board of the party in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I don't know when this happened, but Osman Brka was in Sanski Most in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D00009, 1D9, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you do know that the meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes, but I wasn't there because the president of the Executive Board of Bosanska Krupa was killed in a traffic accident and I attended his funeral that day. But I do know about the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see that the meeting took place on the 16th of March, 1992? Can you confirm that? We can all tell that, can we not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, I did say that the meeting took place, but I don't know if that was the date. It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that on the 18th of March we achieved, in Konak, in Sarajevo, an agreement all three sides with regard to the Cutileiro Plan that three cantons or three constituent units should be established in Bosnia-Herzegovina two days after the meeting, this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, I don't know when it took place, but I did learn of the Cutileiro Plan from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now please look at the agenda and I can read it out for you if you have difficulties with your eyesight. Under 1, report on the current political and security situation in the republic. And under 2, the functioning of the SDA. Can you tell us why were these meetings taking place in the Islamic religious community since they were party meetings?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you right away that the meeting took place in the building of the workers' university where all of us, including the Serbs and Croats, met and not in the Islamic religious community. And let me tell you, even if it had been held in the Islamic religious community, I don't see anything wrong with that. The Islamic religious community did not have the appropriate rooms for such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the text does say that the meeting took place there. Could it not have left the impression with the Serbs that this was some sort of a secret meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you have a look at the text below the date. It says here in the premises of the building of IVZ. Does it not stand for the Islamic religious community?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I told you that it wasn't held there, but I don't even see that it would have been problem if it had been held there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page. If we could -- well, the others can follow the text in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we can keep the Serbian version for you to read.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Do you need the English on the screen? [Interpretation] Could the OTP and the Trial Chamber have the English version and the witness only the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are following the English version on our personal computers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at the following portion. Osman Brka reads, and I'll read from English: [In English] "... Has everything that was supposed to happen really happened. I must say that all of this is absolutely necessary. We could have been destroyed as a people and that is why we took this stand. The space opened for democracy in the areas of the former Yugoslavia has enabled for the historic Muslim issue to be resolved in a just way. The awakening of the people, Muslim people, is in full swing relating to one's own religion and tradition, it is becoming more and more evident. The Muslims in the areas where they have been a minority amongst the Serbs went through the most difficult times. It is important to become organised. With the help of Allah and Alija Izetbegovic we will eventually come out of this chaos as moral and ultimate victors. The fact ..." and so on and so forth. [Interpretation] So the SDA position was that the Muslim people was awakening and that it should reach its goal. What was the goal of the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: A united and independent Bosnia-Herzegovina where all three peoples would live together, namely, the Croats, the Serbs, and the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But of course, in order for that marriage to work, there had to have been the consent of the Serbs as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, of course. I have to smile at what you're saying. And my apologies to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And was there the consent of the Serbs for the idea of leaving Yugoslavia and living in an independent Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I am addressing the Chamber now. The questions you are putting to me are nonsensical and they are common knowledge. Of course there was no consent on the part of the Serb people to leave Yugoslavia, of course there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's see what Mr. Brka has to say further down. He says that there would be -- there would be more victims and there would be trouble, but in return we will get what we want. Conflict is possible but, day to day, it is growing less likely. The world has understood who wants what and so on. And then he goes on to say that Alija Izetbegovic, Silajdzic and Ganic are doing their job well. And then on the next page in Serbian he says that the legal army, we have to gain time and procrastinate. At the time you went to Sarajevo to consult Mr. Izetbegovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Let me tell you, seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this was on the 16th. And on the 19th you went to Sarajevo, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Which month?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: March.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Possible. Possible. I think that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 19th of March, when you were together with the late Mr. Izetbegovic, did you receive information on the agreement that had been reached on the 18th of March?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes, in principle. It was touched upon briefly. Do you think that Mr. Izetbegovic had that much time that he could spend as much as we wanted him to spend with us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you received information that Bosnia would look differently. Were you told at the time that it was a true, genuine, agreement or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Let me tell you, he didn't really tell us anything about it. He wanted to hear our opinion on occasion, wanted to hear the opinion of as many of us as possible, and he never revealed his decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is why I'm interested in this, Mr. Karabeg. If, on the 19th of March, you were informed that an agreement had been reached on the future form of Bosnia to which we agreed that such a Bosnia could secede from Yugoslavia, providing that it had the form that was agreed on the 18th of March, did you go back to Sanski Most thinking that it was all a trick or that it would indeed be that way?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I went to Sanski Most in fear. I had to pass through all those check-points. I was arrested in Mrkonjic with Redzo. We were taken away, mistreated, and interrogated for five hours. Therefore, I really had no time to formulate my opinion and to reflect on that. Moreover, I think that it was Ramadan and Redzo and I were on fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Upon learning that three ethnic communities agreed that Bosnia would be independent in the then-existing borders and that it would have three constituent units, did you stop the campaign of arming and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has just said that he didn't know much about the disagreement and Mr. Karadzic is now putting words into his mouth as to what he did know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very much so, and still complaining about the shortage of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Quite, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Move on to your next topic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, with all due respect, if the witness was there one day after the agreement and they did continue with their war preparations in Sanski Most despite of that, that's quite an important piece of information. And I want to obtain it from the witness. Whether after the 19th of March they stopped with war preparations in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What preparations? I told you what happened. We were arrested and mistreated for five hours, just as you are mistreating me now here as I'm giving evidence to this Court. I asked you, do you really think that Alija had time to talk to us as much as we wanted and when we wanted? It was just coincidental that I as the president of the Executive Board of the municipality went to visit waterworks in Sarajevo and then I stopped by to see whether there was anything new there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Karabeg, please put a pause between the questions and answers. And, Mr. Karadzic, please bear in mind that cross-examination is not an opportunity to argue with the witness. Put your question and you had heard the answer and please get on with it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you to look at --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we need to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are in private session, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, do you see here that a conclusion was reached to set up the Crisis Staff and that Mr. Sabic was tasked with it, and then Sabic goes on to say that you were all well organised and that the headquarters had been informed. Do you see what it says here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here at the top it says -- when did you set up the Crisis Staff in Sanski Most and when did you do that in the surrounding villages and local communes?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Never. I would like to know what is this document that you're putting to me, what is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are minutes of the SDA meeting held in the premises of the Islamic religious community during the visit of Osman Brka, we're still working on the same document.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I repeat that I was not present, that this meeting was not held in the premises of the Islamic religious community, and I don't know what you want from me when it comes to these documents. What is it specifically that I'm supposed to tell you in respect of what is before me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, was Mr. Sead Sabic in charge of setting up the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. This is very minor, but can we show the first page to the witness, top. I take it this is the minutes of the SDA, the 7th Session of the Executive Board of the SDA, and it is noted here that it was held on the premises of the IVZ, but the English translation says IVZ means Executive Council of the Association. But Mr. Karadzic is repeating that it is some Islamic foundation or something. Could you help us in that regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you, these are the minutes of the 7th Session of the Executive Board of the SDA in Sanski Most. It does say here "IVZ," which does stand for the Islamic religious community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we go back to page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What it says here, what Mr. Sabic says. "We have already informed the headquarters with a lot of information. We thought that we would receive from the headquarters some weaponry. It is not a good time to keep silent about the current situation. We have to take a responsible attitude towards the arming. I think that Sanski Most is being neglected by the headquarters." So tell us, please, did they continue with arming in the second half of March?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, how could they have done it when you came in with the 6th Brigade and the entire Sanski Most was divided. The citizens were unable to move about. As for the weapons, I'm not denying that people obtained weapons, procured weapons, on their own, seeing what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Until it comes up, did they conceal anything from you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would help with Mr. Karadzic if he's going to quote what's in the document to actually put where the quotes are starting and also where they're finishing because I don't know whether it's part of the document or it's Mr. Karadzic's comment at the end of the part that he's reading out because I don't have the English -- I don't appear to have the English translation of what's being read out. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that this was a short one so that I was able to follow in my case, but I see your point what you just submitted. So I take it that Mr. Karadzic will heed to your advice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at who is proposing this at the -- the name at the top, Rasim something. He's proposing to get in touch with police commander, commander of the TO, ensure weapons and units, ensure Territorial Defence units, gather the Crisis Staff so that they could give proposals, get together the defence ministry, I guess their offices, organise ourselves, and have a meeting of the Crisis Staff and subunits.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I can make out some words, TO and so on. All of this was supposed to be joined. The municipal defence secretariat was not headed either by a Bosniak or a Croat, but by a Serb. His name was Mladen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether we need to still be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I was about to ask the reason for that, but I forgot. What was the reason why we should be in private session, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We go back to open session and we will lift the confidentiality as well as the video and audio of the previous part. Thank you for your reminder, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Except for just the last discussion that we've just had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very correct. Yes. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. This suits the Defence better. I'm just trying to be cautious and not cause any difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you were a prominent member of the SDA, you were one of the founders, and the Serb side considered you one of the more extreme individuals, as you have put it yourself. Now, let us put aside whether they were right or not. Do you understand that, given what they believed, they suspected you and your actions, some of the things you did?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Let me tell you this. The Serb side had this policy whereby some 200 or 250 of us were declared to be extremists. They said that those 250 extremists, had it not been for them, we could live together with Muslims and Croats. And among those 250 there were Muslims and Croats. Some of them -- some of us were killed, some were put in prison, in Betonirka, and so on, and some were deported to Manjaca. And when we disappeared, the 250 of us, they said again that had it not been for extremists things would have been better. So this is how it was, from the 25th of May until the 10th of October of 1995, this was their main theme. They killed 250 elderly people about a month before Sanski Most was liberated. This is what I wish to say about what they termed "extremists." As for the SDA, yes, I'm one of the first founders of the party.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we leave this document, could we zoom in. Osman Jukanovic. They speak about subunits subbranches, Vrhpolje, Tomina, Caplje, Husimovci, Trnova, and Sehrevci and Pobrijezje. Could we see the lower third of the page, the lower third. It says here that they agreed that self protection should be set up in these places Vrhpolje, Tomina, Kijevo -- could we scroll down to see the other names of villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are these the villages where you said that people organised themselves, Vrhpolje, Tomina, Kijevo, Caplje, Husimovci, Trnova, and so on?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes, yes. These are the villages with majority of Muslim population except for Tomina. I don't know what you mean by self-defence of that population which was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Karabeg, this does not seem to be the case of self organisation but, rather, the result of an order from the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, you are free to hold views as you please and to interpret things as you please. All of these and can we please -- all these are documents taken from the diary of - what's his name? - Nedeljko Rasula. He relied on these issues and insinuated things as his documents and his evidence against us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, sir, these are the minutes of your own party, not his.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: No, these are not our minutes. These are his notes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that this interpretation is not -- it is not one done by the CLSS but by Defence team. Is my understanding correct, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it has a number, the translation has an ERN number. It's a draft summary so it must be a translation of the OTP, or rather, the service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it. Yes, Ms. Sutherland, can you help us in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can certainly look up the MIF to -- because the English translation has an ERN number on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's a full translation. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1678, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, Mr. Reid informs me that it's an AID translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, you were able to see in that book that they were complaining about the military security and state security having been aware of these preparations that were underway. So do you agree that the Serbs were well aware of what their neighbour -- Muslim neighbours, Muslims, were doing as they were preparing for battle?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: What preparations for battle?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have D5 just briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting for that to come up --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- the MIF for the previous document says it's a summary translation so we will have the document checked, and if it's not a full translation, we'll advise the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, look at this, on the 7th of March, one Milos, an intelligence operative, reports about the fact that several individuals were spotted in Sanski Most wearing the uniforms of the Green Berets, that they carried semi-automatic or automatic rifles, that they bore the insignia of the crescent and Islamic symbol. It was assumed that 3.000 citizens of Muslim ethnicity were in possession of long-barrelled weapons. And the main proponents of these activities on behalf of the SDA were Ismet Saracevic, lawyer; Suad Sabic, lawyer; Adil Draganovic, president of a court; Revzid or Resid Kurbegovic, president of the SDA board; Mirzet Karabeg, president of the Executive Board of Sanski Most, et cetera. Can you not see here that already on the 7th of March the Serbs were well aware of what was coming, of what was brewing?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: I don't know what sort of report this is. Is this true at all? Whose report is this? What sort of a report is it? I told you that people at Hrustovo and Vrhpolje organised themselves. Now, what you did throughout the period up until the month of October 1995, what was it you were doing all that time? The questions you are putting now to me deal with I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, the problem here is that participants in a joint government, senior officials such as president of the court, president of -- or the prime minister, local prime minister, are putting together the Green Berets, procuring weapons, arming people, getting consulted on these issues and the Serbs are fully aware of it all throughout that time. What do you expect them to do?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this: If this is indeed what we were doing, how many Serbs lost their lives in that period of time? Why don't you ask me that? And how many Serbs and Croats were taken prisoner and killed? Was there a single Serb who was taken prisoner and who could he have been taken prisoner by? If indeed, as you put it, we had so many things and had procured so many things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why don't you put the question of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was only making -- going to make the observation that Mr. Karadzic puts the document to the witness. He said I don't know what sort of report this is, whose report this is, what sort of a report it is, and then went on to say a few sentences. And then Mr. Karadzic just says the problem here is that -- and then goes on, when he could actually advise the witness what the report is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's time to adjourn for today. Yes. Mr. Karadzic, I would like to recommend you to have a word how to conduct your cross-examination more efficiently with Mr. Robinson. We'll rise for today and continue tomorrow at 9.00. Mr. Karabeg, probably you have been briefed about it, but you are not supposed to discuss about your testimony with anybody else. Do you understand, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of September, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 25
